clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within the following year: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother every evening; your father took night shifts and distanced from your mother; your uncle Anton drank at lunch and was warned at work, then separated from Celeste; your mother's anxiety rose over Anton, and your brother Callum had ear infections through the winter. These shifts pile up from February through May 1979, each touching the next, until your grandmother took a job at the library in May and her functioning lifted.

clusters.name: Odette's bed rest, 1984

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis in September 1986, over the following decade: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and all her appointments; your father phoned his father every night for news of her, then argued with Uncle Lyle over who should help their parents; your grandfather developed chest pains; your father drank most evenings and fought with your mother over his time at his parents' house. Shifts pile up at intervals through 1993, with your grandmother's functioning falling again in 1995 and your grandfather giving up his workshop in February 1996 to stay at her side. The period settles when she moved to the Fairlie nursing home in June 1997.

clusters.name: Callum's move north, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum's leaving home for the mines in May 1999: your father and Callum argued most nights over his plans to go north; your mother could not settle at the thought of him so far away; your father missed days at work and sat up late in the garage; your sister Ines skipped school most of that autumn; your mother took Ines with her everywhere, even to work. Shifts pile up from January through October 1999, each touching the next, until Ines was back at school full days and passed her exams by August 2000.
